question (c): is HIF-1alpha activity protective in neurons?
model: mouse, forebrain-predominant deletion (CaMKIIalpha-Cre line CAMCRE), bilateral carotid occlusion and 7% O2
manipulation (what the HIF arm did): genetic loss of HIF-1alpha in neurons
result for the direction of HIF activity: HARMFUL (loss is protective): neuronal damage lower; apoptosis genes down; no baseline phenotype; most hypoxia-induced genes unchanged (redundancy).

model: mouse, neuron-specific deletion (two CaMKIIalpha-Cre lines), transient MCAo
manipulation (what the HIF arm did): genetic loss of HIF-1alpha in neurons; PHD-inhibiting drugs (DFO and others) in WT and KO
stage / age: adult (Cre active about E18 or about P5)
result for the direction of HIF activity: PROTECTIVE: infarct about 35% larger at 4 d, mortality higher; the drugs' induction of Vegf and Glut-1 and part of their protection depend on neuronal HIF-1alpha; hypoxic tolerance preserved in KO; KO mice viable, 'normal body and brain weight', no obvious behavioural change; hydrocephalus rare.
locator: 'neuronal HIF-1α performs an important role regarding cell survival under ischemic conditions'; 'As adults, they had normal body and brain weight and did not show any obvious alteration in behavior'
transfer caveat for a WWOX-deficient dev: acute injury, adult; opposite sign to c1 in the same kind of model
